newsitem.title: CAYMAN ISLANDS: American tourists arrested for theft in Caymans.
newsitem.headline: American tourists arrested for theft in Caymans.

text.p: A Caribbean cruise vacation came to an abrupt end for three U.S. women when they were arrested for theft on the Cayman Islands.
The three, from Jacksonville, Florida, were arrested Friday and will appear in court Monday, police said. Their names were withheld until then.

They allegedly tried to steal a large amount of money from a store owner in George Town, capital of this upscale British territory, police inspector John Harrington said. He declined to say how much money was involved but said it was "substantial."
One woman was 52 and the other two were in their 30s, he said. They were being held in the police jail until their court appearance.
The women arrived in the Caymans on Friday morning on board the cruise ship Crown Monarch, police said.
A conviction for theft under Cayman law carries a maximum sentence of two years and a fine of up to $12,500.
